chunks: From him, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman whose hair is long; when she prostrates, part of her forehead touches the ground while the rest is covered by her hair. Is that permissible? He said, 'No, until she places her forehead on the ground.'
ai.seo_question: Does long hair invalidate the prostration in prayer if it covers part of the forehead?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarates the condition of *khusu'* and physical completeness in *sujud* by specifying that hair must not obstruct the forehead's contact with the ground. In Shia jurisprudence, this reinforces the principle that the forehead (*jibha*) must be fully exposed and touching the prostration surface, distinguishing it from mere proximity. It highlights the meticulous attention to ritual purity and form in the Shia tradition of prayer.
